delete.consequenceLists: Watchlist + custom lists owned by the user's profiles are soft-deleted.

account.dangerHelper: Removing the user soft-deletes them and cascades cleanup across watch progress + lists.

hls.title: HLS cache
hls.subtitle: Cached transcoded segments live under the cache root. Clear them when you've changed a transcode setting and want every future play to re-encode from scratch.

occupancy.title: Occupancy
occupancy.subtitle: Bytes on disk vs the configured ceiling — the evictor starts dropping LRU buckets once usage exceeds the cap.

clear.title: Clear every HLS cache bucket?
clear.body: Every cached playlist, segment and subtitle generated for this server is removed. The next play of any movie will re-encode from scratch.
clear.consequenceWipe: Every per-source bucket under the cache root is removed.
clear.consequenceRetranscode: The first play of every movie will trigger a fresh ffmpeg pass (slower start, normal afterwards).
clear.consequenceMarker: The last-cleared timestamp updates to now.

health.title: Health
health.subtitle: Live readiness probes for every backing dependency the API needs to serve requests.

settings.title: Runtime settings
settings.subtitle: Operational tunables persisted in the database. Edits propagate to consumers within seconds — no restart required.
settings.propagationNote: Changes flush the snapshot cache immediately; downstream consumers (HLS, scheduler, intro detection) pick them up on their next read. Avatar storage directory is the lone exception — it lazy-caches at startup, so changes require a restart and a manual move of existing files.

errors.minLessThanMax: Min must be less than max.

scheduler.title: Scheduler
scheduler.subtitle: Master switch for every periodic job (library scans, thumbnail backfill, intro detection). Off here means no job ticks at all, regardless of its per-job switch.

enabled.label: Enabled
enabled.helper: Off disables the entire scheduler. Per-job switches below still apply when this is on.

reconcile.label: Reconcile interval
reconcile.helper: How often APScheduler re-reads library schedules from the database. Lower picks up edits sooner; higher reduces idle DB chatter.

thumbnailBackfill.title: Thumbnail backfill
thumbnailBackfill.subtitle: Periodic job that fills in scrub-preview sprites for items the operator hasn't streamed yet.

enabled.label: Enabled
enabled.helper: Toggle the backfill loop. The scheduler master switch must also be on for this to tick.

cadence.label: Cadence
cadence.helper: Lower batch size smooths CPU spikes; higher catches up faster on a fresh catalog.

subdir.label: Subdirectory
subdir.helper: Path (relative to each media file's parent folder) where sprite + VTT pairs are written.

introDetection.title: Intro detection
introDetection.subtitle: Chromaprint-based detector for series intros. Requires the fpcalc binary on PATH on the server.

enabled.label: Enabled
enabled.helper: Toggle the detection loop. The scheduler master switch must also be on for this to tick.

cadence.label: Cadence
cadence.helper: Each season triggers ffmpeg + fpcalc per episode, so values above 2 can saturate the host on large seasons.

audioWindow.label: Audio window
audioWindow.helper: Leading audio analysed per episode. 600 s covers all common cold-open + intro lengths; trim lower to speed up at the cost of missing late intros.

matching.label: Matching
matching.helper: Confidence + per-hash Hamming distance + consecutive-miss tolerance. Tune cautiously — these settings were calibrated against real-world detections.

bounds.label: Length bounds
bounds.helper: Detections outside this range are dropped (too short = stinger, too long = shared underscore bleeding past the title).

streaming.title: Streaming
streaming.subtitle: ffmpeg parallelism cap + HLS cache ceiling. Applies to HLS transcoding, subtitle extraction, and scrub-preview sprite generation.

threads.label: ffmpeg threads
threads.helper: Caps worker threads per ffmpeg invocation. Off leaves ffmpeg in auto (uses every logical core). Set to roughly cpu_count / 2 to cap transcoding to ~50 % of the host. Caps parallelism, not absolute CPU — use cgroups or equivalent for a hard limit.

cacheCap.label: HLS cache cap
cacheCap.helper: Maximum cache directory size. The LRU evictor drops least-recently-accessed buckets once usage exceeds this. Bump on large catalogs to avoid re-transcoding popular titles.
cacheCap.unlimited: 0 disables eviction — cache grows without bound.

avatar.title: Profile avatars
avatar.subtitle: Output location and sizing for uploaded profile avatars.

storageSubdir.label: Storage subdirectory
storageSubdir.helper: Path (relative to the thumbnails directory) where uploaded WebP avatars are written. Lazy-cached at startup.

sizing.label: Sizing
sizing.helper: Max upload size + final square side length after resize. 256 px is the size the picker renders at 1×; bumping it lets the picker render crisper at 2× / 3×.

avatar.subdirMigrationWarning: Changing the storage subdirectory requires an app restart and a manual move of existing avatar files. The path takes effect for new uploads only.

scanDedup.title: Scan deduplication
scanDedup.subtitle: Runtime-delta thresholds for the post-enrich conflict detector. A duplicate is flagged as a suspected different edit only when its runtime delta exceeds BOTH bounds.

thresholds.label: Different-edit thresholds
thresholds.helper: A pair whose runtime delta stays within either bound is treated as the same release. Both must be exceeded to suggest a Director's Cut / Theatrical split.

fallback.label: Title + year fallback
fallback.helper: When on, also flags duplicates by normalized original title + year — catching entries whose enrichment never locked a TMDB id. These weaker matches always go to the queue and are never auto-merged.

conflicts.title: Content conflicts
conflicts.subtitle: Pairs of titles flagged as the same content by the post-enrich detector. Resolve each one as intentionally distinct, replace, or merge keeping both files as variants.

dialog.title: Mark conflicts as distinct
dialog.body: Mark the {{count}} selected conflicts as intentionally distinct?
dialog.consequence1: The detector won't re-queue these pairs on future enrichment passes.
dialog.consequence2: No movies are deleted — both titles in each pair stay in the catalog.

empty.title: No pending conflicts
empty.subtitle: Every detected duplicate has been resolved or none has been flagged yet.
empty.auditTitle: Nothing in the audit log yet
empty.auditSubtitle: Resolved entries appear here once the operator (or the auto-merge detector) closes them.

dialog.title: Resolve conflict
dialog.body: Pick the disposition for this pair. Merge actions soft-delete the losing movie and update cross-context references; mark-as-distinct is a no-op for the data itself.
dialog.irreversibleWarning: Merge actions soft-delete the loser and cannot be undone from this UI.

mark_distinct.description: The pair is intentionally different; the detector won't re-queue it.

merge_replace.description: Keep the winner only; the loser is soft-deleted and its file variants are desreferenced.

merge_keep_both.description: Transfer the loser's file variants to the winner before soft-deleting; the player can pick the best stream at playback time.

snack.failed: Couldn't resolve this conflict. Please try again.

dismiss.consequenceRecreatable: Members can re-create the request later from the same TMDB title.
